canonical_question: What is the specific crystallographic orientation or grain size of the CrTaO4 phase that contributes to the 'uniformity' of the film in the Cr1 alloy?

question_variants.question: What is the specific crystallographic orientation or grain size of the CrTaO4 phase that contributes to the 'uniformity' of the film in the Cr1 alloy?
question_variants.resolution_summary: The text states that the Cr1 alloy has the highest oxide diffraction peak, indicating a uniform and dense oxide film. However, it does not provide specific crystallographic orientation or grain size data for the CrTaO4 phase that contributes to this uniformity.

answers.answer: The text notes: 'the Cr 1 alloy has the highest oxide diffraction peak, indicating that more oxides are generated, making the oxide film on the coating surface uniform and dense'. No specific orientation or grain size is mentioned.
answers.measurement_outcome: Highest oxide diffraction peak, uniform and dense film
answers.boundary_limitation: Crystallographic details of CrTaO4 phase are not provided
evidence_spans: Previous studies focused on mechanical properties at high- and room-temperatures, but with little research and analysis on high-temperature oxidation resistance [ [7] , [8] , [9] ].

The research shows that adding the proper amount of Al, Cr, and Si elements into the refractory high-entropy alloy can form a dense oxidation film on the surface of the alloy in a high-temperature environment, thus improving the high-temperature oxidation resistance [ [10] , [11] , [12] , [13] ].
Unfortunately, elements Al, Cr, and Si very easily form brittle intermetallic compounds with other refractory elements, resulting in reduced mechanical properties of RHEAs [ [14] , [15] , [16] ].
